# 0004: Defensive parsing of ALB headers

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-16
- **Modules:** upload-service, local
- **Source:** design doc, section "How the service trusts ALB headers" (linked from README.md in this folder)

## Decision

Parse defensively, all of it inside one component. It is safe whichever way the ALB behaves, and the NetworkPolicy
(app port from the ALB subnets only) is the second layer, since anything else in the VPC could send forged headers.

## Rules for agents

Only `trust/AlbHeaderTrust` reads `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` or `X-Forwarded-For`, and header names come from config.

1	# Lab results with real phones, 2026-10-16
2	
3	Phones: VVX 250 (firmware 6.4.6), Edge E220 (8.2.3), and a VVX 301 (5.9.x) for the TLS check only. No CCX was
4	available. Uploaded bodies were deleted after the session because they held real call history. Each row names the
5	decision it settled.
6	
7	| Check | Result | What it changed |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Content-Length | Always sent, never chunked. `Expect: 100-continue` on every PUT. No Content-Range. | Keep the 411 rule; the service and the ALB must handle 100-continue (ADR 0009). |
10	| MAC in the certificate | Subject CN, 12 hex digits, uppercase, no separators. No SAN. File names carry the MAC in lowercase. | Read the MAC from the CN and compare case-insensitively (ADR 0004). |
11	| TLS | TLS 1.2 only on all three phones. Shared ciphers: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384. | The ALB policy must allow these on TLS 1.2 (ADR 0003). |
12	| Certificate chain | Phones send 3 certificates (leaf and 2 intermediates); with the root the chain is 4. Device certificates are valid for 15 years. | Exactly at the ALB depth limit of 4, so it must be tested on a real ALB. Phones made before about late 2011 may carry expired certificates; how the ALB treats them is open. |
13	| Reaction to status codes | Retry only on 503: 3 tries, 1 s apart, identical body. Retry-After ignored. 405, 429, 413, 411, 400 and 403 get one try. A 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves app.log stuck for 300 s and holds back the phone's other uploads. | Always reject before 100 Continue. Never 503; prefer 429 when overloaded (ADR 0009). Keys must cope with identical calls.xml copies within 2 s (ADR 0011). |
14	| File names | `<mac>-app.log`, `<mac>-boot.log` (VVX only), `<mac>-calls.xml`. Manual upload: `<mac>-now-app.log`, `<mac>-now-boot.log`; `-now-` comes right after the MAC. | Accept `-now-` after the MAC. Don't require boot.log; the Edge never sends it (ADR 0007). |
15	| What each upload holds | app.log holds only the lines added since the last successful upload, plus any failed lines. `-now-` files and calls.xml are full copies every time. | Store the pieces; joining them in order rebuilds the log. Expect one full app.log per phone at migration. Nothing is lost on a 429. |
16	| Backlog after an outage | After a 15-minute outage the phone sends nothing until something new happens. No log lines or call-list changes were lost. A 1-5-9 call made during the outage was dropped. | No upload flood when the service comes back. |
17	| Other models | The Edge E220 behaves like the VVX 250 except it never sends boot.log and offers only 6 GCM ciphers. The VVX 301 matches the VVX 250 on TLS. | One design fits all three. |
18	| Sizes | app.log 283 B to 28.6 KB; calls.xml 18.5 to 64.8 KB. Every upload took under 35 ms on the LAN. No core dumps seen. | Small bodies. Core-dump sizes come from production data only (`2026-10-15-oci-measurements.md`). |
19	
20	Still open from the lab: whether the ALB accepts the phone's chain at depth 4, whether it overwrites client-sent
21	`X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers (ADR 0004 is safe either way), and how it treats expired device certificates. These need a
22	real ALB, not the Envoy stand-in in `local/`.
23

Phones: VVX 250 (firmware 6.4.6), Edge E220 (8.2.3), and a VVX 301 (5.9.x) for the TLS check only. No CCX was
available. Uploaded bodies were deleted after the session because they held real call history. Each row names the
decision it settled.

| Check | Result | What it changed |
|---|---|---|
| Content-Length | Always sent, never chunked. `Expect: 100-continue` on every PUT. No Content-Range. | Keep the 411 rule; the service and the ALB must handle 100-continue (ADR 0009). |
| MAC in the certificate | Subject CN, 12 hex digits, uppercase, no separators. No SAN. File names carry the MAC in lowercase. | Read the MAC from the CN and compare case-insensitively (ADR 0004). |
| TLS | TLS 1.2 only on all three phones. Shared ciphers: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384. | The ALB policy must allow these on TLS 1.2 (ADR 0003). |
| Certificate chain | Phones send 3 certificates (leaf and 2 intermediates); with the root the chain is 4. Device certificates are valid for 15 years. | Exactly at the ALB depth limit of 4, so it must be tested on a real ALB. Phones made before about late 2011 may carry expired certificates; how the ALB treats them is open. |
| Reaction to status codes | Retry only on 503: 3 tries, 1 s apart, identical body. Retry-After ignored. 405, 429, 413, 411, 400 and 403 get one try. A 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves app.log stuck for 300 s and holds back the phone's other uploads. | Always reject before 100 Continue. Never 503; prefer 429 when overloaded (ADR 0009). Keys must cope with identical calls.xml copies within 2 s (ADR 0011). |
| File names | `<mac>-app.log`, `<mac>-boot.log` (VVX only), `<mac>-calls.xml`. Manual upload: `<mac>-now-app.log`, `<mac>-now-boot.log`; `-now-` comes right after the MAC. | Accept `-now-` after the MAC. Don't require boot.log; the Edge never sends it (ADR 0007). |
| What each upload holds | app.log holds only the lines added since the last successful upload, plus any failed lines. `-now-` files and calls.xml are full copies every time. | Store the pieces; joining them in order rebuilds the log. Expect one full app.log per phone at migration. Nothing is lost on a 429. |
| Backlog after an outage | After a 15-minute outage the phone sends nothing until something new happens. No log lines or call-list changes were lost. A 1-5-9 call made during the outage was dropped. | No upload flood when the service comes back. |
| Other models | The Edge E220 behaves like the VVX 250 except it never sends boot.log and offers only 6 GCM ciphers. The VVX 301 matches the VVX 250 on TLS. | One design fits all three. |
| Sizes | app.log 283 B to 28.6 KB; calls.xml 18.5 to 64.8 KB. Every upload took under 35 ms on the LAN. No core dumps seen. | Small bodies. Core-dump sizes come from production data only (`2026-10-15-oci-measurements.md`). |

content.content:
1	# upload-service architecture
2	
3	How the service is put together and why. The rules are in `CLAUDE.md`, the settings in `CONFIGURATION.md`, and each
4	"why" links to its record in `docs/architecture/decisions/`.
5	
6	## The request path
7	
8	1. The phone opens TLS to the ALB and presents its factory certificate. The ALB checks it against the Poly CAs and
9	   rejects the connection if it fails. Nothing without a valid certificate reaches the service.
10	2. The phone sends `HEAD /logs/<file>` (only before app.log). The service always answers 404: there is never an
11	   existing file to compare against, each upload is self-contained.
12	3. The phone sends `PUT /logs/<file>` with `Expect: 100-continue` and a Content-Length. The ALB adds the
13	   `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-*` headers and appends the phone's IP to `X-Forwarded-For`, then forwards plain HTTP to one
14	   pod.
15	4. `UploadPolicy` runs every check that needs no body, in the order `openapi.yaml` lists: the name parses (400), the type
16	   is enabled (403), the ALB headers identify the caller (403), the certificate MAC equals the file-name MAC (403),
17	   Content-Length is present (411) and within the type's limit (413). The first failure is the answer, sent before 100
18	   Continue so a rejected upload costs no bandwidth (ADR 0009).
19	5. `UploadFlow` builds the key from the server's UTC receive time (`docs/architecture/s3-layout.md`) and streams the body
20	   to S3 with a create-only write (ADR 0011). A collision or a storage failure is 429, never 503.
21	6. Only after S3 confirms does the phone get 200. Nothing else runs on this path.
22	
23	## Packages and how they depend on each other
24	
25	```
26	web ──► upload ──► policy ──► trust
27	          │          │
28	          │          └──► contract (file names, MACs)
29	          ├──► storage (interface) ◄── storage.s3 (the only AWS SDK imports)
30	          └──► metrics
31	config ──► all of the above, validated at startup
32	ratelimit: the RateLimiter interface and InMemoryRateLimiter, not yet called by policy
33	```
34	
35	- `web`: `LogUploadController` (HEAD and PUT), `RejectionStatusMapper` (the one switch from `Rejection` to status),
36	  `RequestLog` (one structured line per request from the same `UploadOutcome` the controller answers with),
37	  `ContinueOnReadCustomizer` (Tomcat sends 100 Continue on first body read, not before).
38	- `trust`: `AlbHeaderTrust` turns the ALB headers into a `ClientIdentity` or an `UntrustedIdentityException`. Last
39	  X-Forwarded-For entry; duplicate mTLS headers rejected; MAC from the leaf's subject CN cross-checked with the Subject
40	  header (ADR 0004).
41	- `policy`: `UploadPolicy` returns a `PolicyDecision`, allowed or rejected with a `Rejection`.
42	- `upload`: `UploadFlow.upload` returns one `UploadOutcome`, `Stored` or `Rejected`, with the duration. `TrackedBody`
43	  wraps the request stream so a body that ends early or stalls becomes `BODY_INCOMPLETE` or `BODY_TIMEOUT`, the same
44	  codes Tomcat already sent.
45	- `storage`: `LogStorage.store(LogObject)` returns `StoreResult.STORED` or `KEY_EXISTS`. `storage.s3.S3LogStorage` is
46	  the only implementation; tests use `InMemoryLogStorage`.
47	- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, one record per group, refuses to start without an entry per `FileType`.
48	- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created. A placeholder today.
49	
50	## Why each choice
51	
52	- Defensive header parsing, and the Spring and cloud8 forwarded-header filters turned off: ADR 0004.
53	- Specific status codes, Content-Length required, never 503, every check before 100 Continue: ADR 0009.
54	- Timeout order S3 60 s < ALB 120 s < Tomcat 130 s, so the phone always hears us and not the ALB: ADR 0005.
55	- The key with no suffix and the create-only write: ADR 0011.
56	- `/logs/**` as a cloud8 public path, everything else still 401: ADR 0006.
57	- Per-pod in-memory rate limit behind an interface: ADR 0010.
58	- calls.xml off until the privacy review: ADR 0008.
59	- The ALB through the common chart ingress, the DigiCert certificate, the TLS policy: ADR 0001, 0002, 0003.
60	- Pod Identity for the S3 role, AWS SDK v2, the herd-endpoints namespace: ADR 0012, 0013, 0015.
61	
62	## What is deliberately not here
63	
64	Customer lookup, parsing and indexing belong to the processor, so a slow lookup can never delay or fail an upload.
65	There is no read API in this repo.
66	
67	## Runtime (designed; the chart is a placeholder)
68	
69	- Chart `device-log-upload-service-chart` on cloud8-common-chart. Ingress from the common chart with class `alb`.
70	  `serviceaccount.yaml` with no role annotation (Pod Identity). `networkpolicy.yaml`: app port from the ALB's subnets
71	  only, since anything else in the VPC could send forged mTLS headers; management port from monitoring.
72	- Probes on `/public/ping`; the ALB health check on the same path. Readiness does not depend on S3, so an S3 blip does
73	  not drain every pod at once.
74	- Shutdown: `server.shutdown: graceful`, a preStop pause covering ALB deregistration, and a termination grace period
75	  longer than the slowest expected upload (start at 150 s).
76	- Scale: at least 3 replicas across zones, HPA on CPU. Uploads are I/O bound, so threads matter more than CPU; the
77	  designed in-flight cap protects each pod.
78	
79	## Status against the design
80	
81	Built: the request path above, the status codes, streaming, the create-only write, the structured log line. Not built:
82	the rate limit and in-flight cap, metrics, the keep-alive and graceful-shutdown settings, the Helm chart, and the file
83	types beyond app.log, boot.log and calls.xml. Each gap is also noted in the ADR it belongs to.
84

# upload-service architecture

How the service is put together and why. The rules are in `CLAUDE.md`, the settings in `CONFIGURATION.md`, and each
"why" links to its record in `docs/architecture/decisions/`.

## The request path

1. The phone opens TLS to the ALB and presents its factory certificate. The ALB checks it against the Poly CAs and
   rejects the connection if it fails. Nothing without a valid certificate reaches the service.
2. The phone sends `HEAD /logs/<file>` (only before app.log). The service always answers 404: there is never an
   existing file to compare against, each upload is self-contained.
3. The phone sends `PUT /logs/<file>` with `Expect: 100-continue` and a Content-Length. The ALB adds the
   `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-*` headers and appends the phone's IP to `X-Forwarded-For`, then forwards plain HTTP to one
   pod.
4. `UploadPolicy` runs every check that needs no body, in the order `openapi.yaml` lists: the name parses (400), the type
   is enabled (403), the ALB headers identify the caller (403), the certificate MAC equals the file-name MAC (403),
   Content-Length is present (411) and within the type's limit (413). The first failure is the answer, sent before 100
   Continue so a rejected upload costs no bandwidth (ADR 0009).
5. `UploadFlow` builds the key from the server's UTC receive time (`docs/architecture/s3-layout.md`) and streams the body
   to S3 with a create-only write (ADR 0011). A collision or a storage failure is 429, never 503.
6. Only after S3 confirms does the phone get 200. Nothing else runs on this path.

## Packages and how they depend on each other

```
web ──► upload ──► policy ──► trust
          │          │
          │          └──► contract (file names, MACs)
          ├──► storage (interface) ◄── storage.s3 (the only AWS SDK imports)
          └──► metrics
config ──► all of the above, validated at startup
ratelimit: the RateLimiter interface and InMemoryRateLimiter, not yet called by policy
```

- `web`: `LogUploadController` (HEAD and PUT), `RejectionStatusMapper` (the one switch from `Rejection` to status),
  `RequestLog` (one structured line per request from the same `UploadOutcome` the controller answers with),
  `ContinueOnReadCustomizer` (Tomcat sends 100 Continue on first body read, not before).
- `trust`: `AlbHeaderTrust` turns the ALB headers into a `ClientIdentity` or an `UntrustedIdentityException`. Last
  X-Forwarded-For entry; duplicate mTLS headers rejected; MAC from the leaf's subject CN cross-checked with the Subject
  header (ADR 0004).
- `policy`: `UploadPolicy` returns a `PolicyDecision`, allowed or rejected with a `Rejection`.
- `upload`: `UploadFlow.upload` returns one `UploadOutcome`, `Stored` or `Rejected`, with the duration. `TrackedBody`
  wraps the request stream so a body that ends early or stalls becomes `BODY_INCOMPLETE` or `BODY_TIMEOUT`, the same
  codes Tomcat already sent.
- `storage`: `LogStorage.store(LogObject)` returns `StoreResult.STORED` or `KEY_EXISTS`. `storage.s3.S3LogStorage` is
  the only implementation; tests use `InMemoryLogStorage`.
- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, one record per group, refuses to start without an entry per `FileType`.
- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created. A placeholder today.

## Why each choice

- Defensive header parsing, and the Spring and cloud8 forwarded-header filters turned off: ADR 0004.
- Specific status codes, Content-Length required, never 503, every check before 100 Continue: ADR 0009.
- Timeout order S3 60 s < ALB 120 s < Tomcat 130 s, so the phone always hears us and not the ALB: ADR 0005.
- The key with no suffix and the create-only write: ADR 0011.
- `/logs/**` as a cloud8 public path, everything else still 401: ADR 0006.
- Per-pod in-memory rate limit behind an interface: ADR 0010.
- calls.xml off until the privacy review: ADR 0008.
- The ALB through the common chart ingress, the DigiCert certificate, the TLS policy: ADR 0001, 0002, 0003.
- Pod Identity for the S3 role, AWS SDK v2, the herd-endpoints namespace: ADR 0012, 0013, 0015.

## What is deliberately not here

Customer lookup, parsing and indexing belong to the processor, so a slow lookup can never delay or fail an upload.
There is no read API in this repo.

## Runtime (designed; the chart is a placeholder)

- Chart `device-log-upload-service-chart` on cloud8-common-chart. Ingress from the common chart with class `alb`.
  `serviceaccount.yaml` with no role annotation (Pod Identity). `networkpolicy.yaml`: app port from the ALB's subnets
  only, since anything else in the VPC could send forged mTLS headers; management port from monitoring.
- Probes on `/public/ping`; the ALB health check on the same path. Readiness does not depend on S3, so an S3 blip does
  not drain every pod at once.
- Shutdown: `server.shutdown: graceful`, a preStop pause covering ALB deregistration, and a termination grace period
  longer than the slowest expected upload (start at 150 s).
- Scale: at least 3 replicas across zones, HPA on CPU. Uploads are I/O bound, so threads matter more than CPU; the
  designed in-flight cap protects each pod.

## Status against the design

Built: the request path above, the status codes, streaming, the create-only write, the structured log line. Not built:
the rate limit and in-flight cap, metrics, the keep-alive and graceful-shutdown settings, the Helm chart, and the file
types beyond app.log, boot.log and calls.xml. Each gap is also noted in the ADR it belongs to.

The upload service defends against forged `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers in two layers, plus a third that only exists locally.

**1. Defensive parsing in one class (ADR 0004).** Only `trust/AlbHeaderTrust` reads `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` or `X-Forwarded-For`, and the header names come from config. The design assumes nothing about whether the ALB overwrites headers a client sent itself:
- Each of Subject, Issuer, Validity, Serial-Number and Leaf must appear exactly once. Zero or two copies is a 403, because the service can't tell which copy the ALB wrote.
- The Leaf header must decode from URL-encoded PEM into an X.509 certificate.
- The leaf's subject must have exactly one CN, and it must be 12 uppercase hex digits (the MAC).
- The leaf's CN must match the CN in the Subject header.
- Only the last `X-Forwarded-For` entry is used, since the ALB appends its own address there. Earlier entries are whatever the client sent.
- The Spring and cloud8 forwarded-header filters are turned off, so nothing else interprets these headers.
- All of this runs in `UploadPolicy` before 100 Continue. After it, the certificate MAC must equal the MAC in the file name, or the upload gets a 403.

**2. NetworkPolicy, the second layer.** Only the ALB subnets may reach the app port, because anything else in the VPC could send forged mTLS headers. Note that this layer is designed but not built: `networkpolicy.yaml` holds only a comment, and the chart is listed as a placeholder in "Not built".

**3. Local only: Envoy, the ALB stand-in.** It removes every `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert*` header the client sent before adding its own. This doesn't show what the real ALB does.

**Still unconfirmed** (from the 2026-10-16 lab results): whether the real ALB overwrites `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers a client sent. The same note says ADR 0004 is safe either way. Two related ALB questions are also open: whether it accepts the phones' depth-4 chain, and how it treats expired device certificates. Answering them needs a real ALB, not Envoy.
